title: Question 11
stem:
A bridge rectifier contains four ideal diodes A, B, C and D, as shown in Fig. 11.1.
The output of the rectifier is connected to a load L of resistance 2.4 kΩ.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: On Fig. 11.1, mark with the letter P the positive terminal of the load.

markscheme_points.text: point P shown at ‘lower end’ of load

hints: Hint 1: Focus on the physical mechanism in A Level Physics theory and principles that causes this behavior.
parts.proper_answer: point P shown at ‘lower end’ of load

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The variation with time $t$ of the potential difference $V$ across the input to the rectifier is shown in Fig. 11.2.
Calculate the root-mean-square (r.m.s.) current in the load L.
$$I_{\text{r.m.s.}} = \dots\dots\dots\dots\dots\dots\dots\dots\dots\dots\,\text{A}$$
hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in A Level Physics theory and principles connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
State the core physical principle governing this problem: A level physics theory and principles. Identify the relationship between the given quantities.

Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:
Vr.m.s. = 6.0 / √2 = 4.24 V; Ir.m.s. = 4.24 / (2.4 × 103) = 1.8 × 10-3 A
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.
